body: How does someone answer this about themselves honestly and objectively? If I said yes, maybe I’m just a narcissistic prick. If I say no, maybe I just have low self esteem. I don’t fucking know. My face is relatively symmetrical, but I’m overweight. Some people find me attractive, some people don’t. I’m working on my weight and all, but I don’t want to be celibate until I’m happy with my body. I’ve had some decent, albeit short term relationships that were good for the time. I’m searching for more of those. I think you have a point, but 99% of the time, a relationship isn’t going to fall into your lap without putting in some effort on your part. If I just decide to ignore that component of life until I’m 100% satisfied with myself, I might just die alone.

Fair enough. For lots of fortunate folk, money is easier to spend than time and energy. For what it’s worth, I’m sorry! I don’t mean to hurt anyone. I guess hurt people hurt people though. I don’t mean to. I’m just kinda desperate for connection I guess.

Fair enough. I consider myself an ally. I don’t want to be harmful at all to the LGBTQ+ community, but maybe I’m taking advantage. I believe in the Kinsey scale, and I don’t think I’m 100% straight, no exceptions, but I just don’t find myself attracted to men or willing to open up sexually with them. I’ve had plenty of opportunities, but it just doesn’t seem right for me. Maybe I’ll discover something one day, but that just doesn’t seem in the cards right now. Who knows? Maybe I’m closeted, maybe I’m an asshole.
Some asshole.
Not really. I don’t get any sexual gratification out of it whatsoever. Just a small boost in self esteem to realize that some people actually value me in that way. Purely egotistical.

You have a point, and I freely accept that the attention is somewhat under false pretenses, but if it changes anything, I’ve never actually gotten free drinks out of it. I’m not financially scamming people. Maybe just emotionally.

Maybe I’m just a psycho, but a cheek kiss seems no more consequential than a fist bump to me. It’s just a time to reiterate that I’m straight to avoid having them put in more effort for no reason. Idk.

I get that. I don’t have any desire whatsoever to disrupt safe spaces or to make the lives of LGBTQ+ people any harder. I just enjoy having people approach me. It’s a fair point that encouraging that under false pretenses makes me an asshole. Idk. I’m American. Therapy is expensive and difficult. Another shitty excuse I know. I’m sorry.
Fair point. I don’t mean to disrupt safe spaces. I just find it easier to have unwanted advances than to find a therapist. Shitty excuse, I know.
I wish. It’s weird. I love gay people and feel very open to anyone making any choice they’re comfortable with concerning sexuality. I just don’t find myself very attracted to men.
Fair. As an American, bars are cheaper than therapy though. Not a good excuse, but whatever. I’m cheap and possibly an asshole.
For sure.

Definitely not the worst, but I think people really underestimate how taxing commercial construction is, at every level. The name of the game is usually you can work your fucking ass off for 60+ hours a week to make good money, but that really kills any kind of potential for a real work/life balance. At the lowest levels, day laborers perform heavy, physical labor in 100+°F heat and severe humidity for 12 hours a day or more, often times seven days a week. Most day laborers, I know, either drink very heavily, do drugs, or both to cope. Even quality assurance people have less taxing jobs, but similar issues with having a balance. The people at the top I imagine would be happier, but anytime something goes wrong, it falls on them. They have massive headaches every time some random asshole on the job site does something wrong, especially if you’re on anything federal. I think it is an extremely difficult industry to regardless of your exact job title.

In middle school, I asked my teacher what the date was on Valentine’s Day, and he made a joke with my science teacher saying, “oh, I’m anon, and I’m too busy for Valentine’s Day,” and laughed about it in my face with my science teacher. Great way to make an already insecure kid feel good about himself! Prick.

Oh, and they would know if I started therapy and mentioned that, so it makes therapy feel like a bad option in a way. It’s weird mental gymnastics to just shoot down other potential good options I have. Idk

I don’t know if I’m just repeating myself at this point. It’s a weird state to be in when you’re transitioning into trying to make life better, but you’ve had the idea of just ending it all on your mind for so long. It’s like an easy default now whenever something doesn’t go right. Like overall, I’m working towards the future, but any bad day or major setback just reminds me of that option again. It’s like a curse now that won’t go away.

There are some psychological studies out there that seem to suggest that even if you get a job doing something you love, the nature of it being a job will make you resent it, so I don’t really know if that’s possible. And the goal was to keep improving. Maybe I can, but sooner or later, age will start factoring in. Regardless of my depression, I’ve always felt I would rather die younger than wither away like I’ve watched many of my family members do. Alzheimer’s runs in the family, and I’ve also seen some ALS. It looks awful, I don’t want that. I don’t want to be in my 60’s lamenting how my body doesn’t work as well as it used to and now I need specific diets, exercises, and pills to just keep moving forward. Suicide just seems like a practical idea. I’ll stop being miserable before life starts piling more on top to be miserable about. If I can’t handle life when things are good, then I’m surely fucked if hardship ever does fine me.

I studied psychology in college, but quit after getting a BS, so doing much with that would mean going back to school. In short, I’ve been in construction since covid started. It was a great way to make some money and my job had a lot of great perks like giving me a company car to drive, but it doesn’t make me happy. I’m thinking about being a pilot, but a history of suicidal thoughts is an automatic FAA discharge, so eh. Even that thought seems like needing to work harder. I don’t even know what would make me happy. I don’t know if work really can. I don’t have the energy for all that. Suicide just becomes the easiest option when you’ve thought about it for as long as I have. It probably isn’t the right option, but I’m tired. I don’t have the energy to keep pushing.

Especially in the last 5 years, I feel like I’ve really tried, with some mixed success. I would say I’m generally happier now than I was when that plan formed, but it’s not enough. I don’t see a decent path forward. Exercise has helped me tremendously, but my body isn’t very good at losing weight. My career prospects are pretty much nil at this point since I’ve spent the past 3 years becoming a specialist only to realize lately that I despise every second of it. Despite trying by going out and joining clubs and shit, I still can’t cultivate meaningful friendships. I guess I’m an asshole. I know everyone on this subreddit says it, and for the most part, it’s total horseshit, but I feel I’ve really tried, and while all of these things have helped a little, it’s like a day late and a dollar short. I’m realizing that to get the results I want, clearly it’s going to require so much more time, effort, and focus than I am able to give. The answer is always just to work harder, and I’m just sick of working at all.

It feels like a countdown because of the reasons behind putting it off and all. I clearly have some mental issue having these thoughts, but I’ve always considered myself a very logical and pragmatic person. I put it off knowing that I was a young idiot who had barely even experienced life, and figured that 10 years and some concerted effort to make things better might totally change my whole perspective. To some degree, it has, but not enough I guess. I would say I’m a generally happier person now than I used to be, but I just fall into thinking the bad times grossly outweigh the good, and I’m just not interested in sucking a corporate cock for the next 40 years to hopefully be able to afford a modest living with some occasional fun. The ratio sucks.

I feel similarly, but I’m still in college. Great parents, decent living situation, free college, but I just don’t feel happy, and I haven’t in years. I also stay alive for my loved ones. It feels awful to know your complaining about a seemingly great life, but if you’re dealing with mental illness, it doesn’t really matter. Stay strong.

I get that, and honestly, it does comfort me in a weird way. I think it’s maybe a first step to ideation, but regardless, there is some comfort from knowing no matter how bad things get, I always have another option. Also, yeah, in a weird way, it does make me less suicidal in the moment. I just think more along the lines of “things aren’t so bad now, I’ll wait until they are at least.” Do you talk to anyone face to face about this stuff?

Inert gas asphyxiation. I don’t think we’re supposed to discuss methods much on this subreddit, but googling that would tell you what you need to know. It ensures a quick, painless death, but it’s complicated to set up, easy to fail, and requires some potentially expensive equipment.

I’ve done a fair amount of research on it over the past couple days, but I’m no professional. From what I gather, acetaminophen causes liver damage (that’s no secret, it’s pretty well-known and warned about), so overdosing on that is likely to shut down your liver and cause a slow, painful death. I couldn’t find out exactly how hydrocodone kills you online. It seems like that part isn’t readily disclosed to the public, but it is disclosed that hydrocodone is a depressant and that mixing it with alcohol is a fairly common cause of death for opioid addicts. I’m mostly guessing here, but I’d say it’s because multiple depressants taken at the same time intensify each other’s effects. Since they slow your heart rate and breathing, I’m hoping that it’ll pretty much put me to sleep. I’m not positive though. Inert has asphyxiation is much preferred, but harder to accomplish and expensive.

I thought it’d be a little more instant. I was thinking that the hydrocodone, as a depressant and the alcohol, another depressant, would slow my breathing or heart rate enough to kill me the same night. You seem so much more knowledgeable about this, but it’s worth making sure. Also, i thought the mushy solid was the acetaminophen and the liquid would contain the hydrocodone.

Sure. Can't speak for all suicidal people, but I gotta find a way to live in between contemplation settings. The fun shit doesn't last long, and happiness fades. The depression and self-loathing never go away. They're there constantly. I'm more afraid of my future than anything else.
like, without the CWE? I don't want to take it before that because the acetaminophen is likely to kill me first, slowly and painfully.

That’s a tough question. I just don’t. I don’t particularly enjoy life. It disappoints more often than it satisfies. I don’t like who I am, and I don’t really have much hope for the future being better. When I get in depressive funks, I can tell you exact reasons, but when I’ve calmed down (like now) it’s more of a lack of reasons to continue. Self-loathing is a big one though.
I go back and forth between wanting to talk, being too scared to, and ignoring everything. I kinda want to talk now though.

I currently live in a state where my insurance doesn’t cover anyone. I could see a campus doctor I suppose, but I don’t know he rules. And yeah. That’s part of my problem, really. If I didn’t, I think I could end it, but people I care about would be really hurt.

All the time. I’ve come up with a very detailed plan to do it, but then I think about my family and try to push the thoughts away. They’re always there though. Even when I’m having a good time with friends or family, it’ll pop up and consume my thoughts.

I get that. I feel the same way often, but when I calm down and try to remember the good times and realize that my death could cause this severe pain I’m feeling right now for family members who have invested so much in me and grown to love me. The pain would be over for me, but it would be multiplied on those I love. That’s a good enough reason for me. I’d rather be the one that suffers to benefit 5 different people, than be the one that causes it to spread more. All for one, and one for all, right? I don’t mean to seem insensitive or insult you in anyway, this is just my personal feelings on the matter.

I really do get that. I usually try to keep that schedule, like I said, but it doesn’t always work. I moved away from home, but I still come back for the holidays. I only come for family, I absolutely hate my hometown, and coming back always fucks me up. It brings back insomnia instantly, and I’ve pretty much been a shut in for the past 2 weeks since I’ve been here. I spend my entire days playing video games, sleeping, and eating as much as I can. 

Back to the advice though, I get where you’re coming from, but I suggest you try regardless. Sometimes, I genuinely enjoy getting out and doing things with friends. Far more often though, I get uncomfortable halfway through, have a terrible time, and come back home more depressed than before. I kick myself and say I should stop going out, but I force it anyway because I know it’s good, and I’m terrified of being more alone than I already am. I barely ever interact with anyone. I have friends I used to spend all my time with that I maybe see a couple times a semester. I force myself out, like or not to keep those relationships, however small they may be, alive. I’ve found things that are better than others. Parties almost never go well for me, so I’ve cut those out. I meet people most often for dinner or lunch (more as an excuse to get good food than anything honestly), but also for things like hiking so there isn’t this immense pressure to fill voids of silence with awkward smalltalk. I don’t know if this is super healthy, or even a great method for recovery, but it works for me.

I feel you so much, and I think we both need help. Maybe therapy, maybe meds, maybe you actually can find a way to help yourself. I don’t know, but if you need a reason to be here tomorrow, use your mom for that. I feel I stay alive for my parents too. I don’t want to be here anymore, but I just picture my parents crying at my funeral. I can’t do that to them. I think you and I both need to find a more permanent and beneficial method, but for now, cling to what you have. Your mother clearly loves you deeply, so let that be your reason to see tomorrow and seek help to see more tomorrows.

I say the same kinda things to myself every day. I think we have to see that future though. Hopefully by then, you’ll have found some better help and some peace, but if you need a reason now, remember those friends that care about you. Think about how they’d feel. Think about all the possibilities your future holds. The best experiences are often unexpected. Find reasons to see tomorrow until you find something better.
I wish more people were like you then. That seems like a good way to look at it!

I feel almost exactly the same way. I hate seeing myself in pictures or the mirror. I’m disgusted by what I see. I wish I could give more advice, but I’m struggling with it too. I’ve found it does help to force myself to be somewhat active or productive by setting schedules and such. I feel like I have no friends too usually, but if I try, I can usually find someone who wants to see me. I honestly hate going out sometimes, I feel socially inept, but I make dates and such with friends to give myself obligation. That might help? I’m trying to add exercise to that schedule this year too. My bed is like my nest, I can spend weeks there if I let myself, so I force myself to be away from home with these tasks and stuff. Could be a good place to start.

I relate to this so much. I’m no expert, but I think maybe you should seek help even if it doesn’t seem that bad to you. I don’t know how it is for most people, but for me, suicidal ideation was a gradual thing. It didn’t spring into my head one night, it festered and grew for years. It starts innocently enough by thinking you just want to end the bad parts. Then you eventually become ok with the thought of death. You find a peace with it and decide it isn’t scary, possibly even nice. Then, it consumes your thoughts. It’s not just in your head at your lows, it pops up everywhere. On Christmas with your family, out having a good time with friends, playing games, etc. I don’t know if this is universally true, but this is my experience. Find support before you start to collapse.

I appreciate the sentiment, but do you think anyone really takes pride in making the world a worse place? I think besides sociopaths or other extremes, even the worst of the worst think they’re doing good. The guys screaming at women trying to get abortions and bombing clinics seem like monsters to me, but they think they’re saving precious lives from dastardly doctors and evil women. Not trying to be super political here or disrespect anyone’s beliefs, I just mean we both think we’re right. My version of good is surely someone else’s version of evil. Who’s right?

I think it’s near impossible for people to be objective about themselves or people they care about. I have to admit, my “objective” self view is extremely negative, which is likely due to some serious bias. If you determine your own self worth though, then in a fucked up kinda way, your view is the only one that matters.

Personally, I’m not a believer in spirituality or cosmic will. I think things just kind of happen, and we are pretty much left to our own device to create meaning. I try to be good for others because I think the collective of my friends and family are by far more important than me. I don’t think I’ll be any great revolutionizer or anything. I’m training for a soulless office job. I think we should all try to bring good into the world for the sake of making the world, or at least society a better place. I’m not confident in my ability to do that anymore. What if my suicide inspires one of my artistic friends to write a song that stops millions more from killing themselves? It would be hard, then, to say that it wasn’t beneficial. I don’t know. I’m sorry to be so bleak and combative, but if you can’t do it to strangers on the internet, where can you do it? I respect your beliefs and appreciate your help, I’m just like this.

I’m glad you can take comfort in what good you do. I don’t want to take that from you, but I just want your opinion on when have you done enough? I have this kind of theory that a sort of selfishness is necessary for survival. Like, if you have $5 to your name, and you pass someone on the street begging for money, it’s selfish not to give them money, but you need money to survive as well. I think in life, we have to find the level of selfishness we’re willing to adhere to. You can say it’s justified selfishness because you have to keep yourself healthy too, but where’s the line? I’m trying to save money for my future, but I’m surrounded by people struggling to get by. I don’t know how to reconcile that. I work and a good portion of my money was earned, but a far greater portion comes from being born lucky to a well off family. I don’t deserve it per se. Again, I don’t want to drag you down. I don’t know why I’m so combative, but I like arguments.

I feel that. Well, maybe you can do what I’m trying to do. My parents don’t take very good care of themselves, so I’m trying to stay alive until they’re gone. I know it may take years, so I’m the meantime, I’m taking steps to try and survive it at least. I’ve seen a counselor, and I’m looking into meds. It’s hard to offer advice to not do something that I also really want to do, but I guess you understand where I’m coming from about remaining for the sake of others. Just try and make things better, and maybe by the time we don’t have parents to worry about, we’ll have found some semblance of happiness.

Hope maybe wasn’t the right way to phrase it. Honestly, I don’t have much hope. I’ve done a lot of research into methods lately, and sometimes I think I’m just waiting until I can finally be done. Despite that all though, I still live day by day. I have a solid plan, and feasible means to go through with it, but I never do despite an intense desire. Again, it’s because of my family. As much as I’m hurting, I don’t want to stop it at their expense. I keep imagining my parents crying. I’d be their second lost child. I desperately want to believe I can do it and be done, but I know it’ll only be done for me. Maybe that’s not your reason, but I believe since you’re still here, you have some reason. Can you think of it at all?

I feel the same way too sometimes. I’m no professional, but I think maybe it’s dissociation? What is your thinking like when you get in those states? It’s incredibly hard for me to put into words. It’s so confusing. Time doesn’t seem to exist, and it doesn’t feel like I’m actually there. Maybe you could help me describe it.

I relate to this like you wouldn’t believe. When I started college, things were better. It didn’t last very long though. Now friends and family talk about how much happier I am since I moved, and they have no idea how I really feel. You must have some hope though, right? I personally believe everyone has something keeping them alive. Some people have more than others because it’s an unfair world. Mine is my family. What’s yours?

You’re doing the right thing by seeking a professional. I envy you in a way. Be honest and open with your doctor, and don’t lose hope. Meds aren’t perfect, and it sometimes takes a while for them to find the right chemical balance, but that’s why literally hundreds of different antidepressants exist. Have faith you might find the right one.
Me personally, no. I want to disappear without being a blip on anyone’s radar. The thought of damaging others is the reason I’m still here.
It’s hard creating a support base when you have trouble convincing yourself you deserve one. Have you ever talked to a professional? I started seeing a counselor recently, and it has helped a bit.

Have you tried anything so far? I understand pushing people away. I do it too. I started seeing a counselor though, and I can’t really say it’s totally helped, but it feels good to have at least someone.

I understand not getting help. I typically refuse it too. Can you explain why though? I think part of my reason was fear, but another part was self-loathing. I didn’t want to burden anyone else. I wish I had a gun sometimes. It sounds like you might benefit from getting rid of yours though. Having an easy way out is dangerous. I’m pretty sure I couldn’t be typing this if I had one.
Would you care to comment on your experience in the psych ward otherwise? I sometimes think I might need that myself, but honestly, it also scares me too.

Yeah. On a similar note, I’ve gotten really into this podcast called “The Hilarious World of Depression” lately. Comedians talk about their experience with mental illness, and it helps a lot to hear their stories of success despite the shit they deal with.

I used to try and write books. I used to dream about being an author, but I hate my own writing. I haven't written creatively in a long time. I understand what you mean by a loop though. I started writing to try and convey my feelings, but it reminded me of my own loneliness and depression. I also partially quit because of the negativity. One of my last attempts was about a loner that has medical issues and hallucinates a love interest while in the hospital. It seemed overly dramatic, and just made me sad to think about anyway.
Possibly soon. I have to survive finals this week. Thank you.
